title: Evidence as a primitive: references, evidence, experiments, synthesis
summary: A proposal for the evidence types in the harness corpus, built on markdown-db (S-GFFY), with a survey of prior art and a worked example.

blocks.title: The problem and the constraints
blocks.text:
Evidence is the primitive the rest of the harness corpus builds on. A fact such as "Claude Code does not read AGENTS.md natively" is only as good as what backs it.

Alpha, the frozen prototype, has the parts but not the shape:

- **Evidence is mixed into the claim.** Each observation inside a fact holds both the value (`value`, `since`, `until`) and its backing (`source`, `locator`, `evidence`, `checked_version`).
- **A run leaves no record.** `probes/` hold the commands, but a run's output and date are not kept. Some facts reuse the source's date instead.
- **No excerpt.** What a page said lives in prose or in a research note, not in a field.
- **Unpinned locators.** Sources link to `blob/main`, which changes under the link.

Constraints:

- **S-GFFY v0.** `x-ref` works only on a top-level property or the items of a top-level array. So a claim that points at evidence must be its own record with a top-level `evidence` list, or the standard must grow.
- **Ship a type with a writer.** The dev repo's data-model decision (D-ORMG) deferred its own Evidence entity, and its one donor instance was broken. A type ships with one thing that writes it and one that reads it.
- **No confidence score.** OKF, osdlc's system-model and the survey all argue against a stored score: it invites arithmetic nobody can justify, and it goes stale.
- **Pure data.** Every rule is in a schema or the standard, never only in code.

blocks.title: The cascade: four levels, each built on the one below

rows.label: 0 · Reference
rows.detail: A page, repo or binary we can point at. No claim about what it says.

rows.label: 1 · Evidence
rows.detail: One observation of a reference: what it said or did, when, for which version.

rows.label: 2 · Experiment
rows.detail: A folder with a procedure and fixtures. Each run writes a level-1 record.

rows.label: 3 · Synthesis
rows.detail: A narrative note that argues across many evidence records.

blocks.title: Worked example · "Claude Code does not read AGENTS.md natively" (illustration: URL, excerpt, version and hash are made up, not fetched)

├── references/
│   ├── references.schema.md
│   └── Anthropic/
│       └── Claude Code memory docs.md
├── evidence/
│   ├── evidence.schema.md
│   └── Claude Code/
│       ├── 2026-11-05 memory docs on AGENTS.md.md
│       └── 2026-11-05 run agents-md-read.md
├── experiments/
│   ├── experiments.schema.md
│   └── agents-md-read/
│       ├── agents-md-read.md          the folder record
│       ├── setup.sh

steps.title: Four types, one folder each
steps.summary: `references`, `evidence`, `experiments` and `claims` sit beside `harnesses` in corpus beta.
steps.detail: Each is a type folder holding `<name>.schema.md`, as S-GFFY already requires. Records are named for people: the page title, or the date plus what was looked at.

steps.title: Level 0: the page itself
steps.summary: One record per page, grouped by publisher. Many evidence records can point at it over time.
steps.detail: Holds only what is stable about the page: URL, title, publisher, and an optional Wayback snapshot plus live/dead status. It says nothing about what the page claims.

steps.title: Level 1: what the docs said, on a date

anchor.exact: # evidence/Claude Code/2026-11-05 memory docs on AGENTS.md.md

steps.summary: An observation of the reference: kind, date, version, and the quoted text.
steps.detail: `excerpt` follows the W3C TextQuoteSelector: the exact words plus a little text either side, so a re-check can tell whether the quote is still on the page, moved, or gone. `version_basis: inferred` because a docs page does not say which release it describes.

steps.title: Level 1: what a run showed
steps.summary: Same type, `kind: run`. Points at the experiment, not at a reference.
steps.detail: The run block borrows from RO-Crate and MLflow: run id, environment, outcome, transcript path and hash. The record is written once and not edited; a later run that disagrees is a new record.

steps.title: Level 2: the experiment is a folder
steps.summary: A folder record: its markdown file has the folder's name, everything else in the folder belongs to it.
steps.detail: Popper-style stages: `setup`, `run`, `validate`, `teardown`. `validate.sh` turns raw output into a verdict per claim.

steps.title: A negative claim needs a positive control
steps.summary: The run proves CLAUDE.md is read, so "AGENTS.md was not read" means something.
steps.detail: Without the control, a broken test and a real "not read" look the same.

steps.title: The claim points at its evidence
steps.summary: A claim is its own record with a top-level `evidence` list, which S-GFFY v0 can check with `x-ref`.
steps.detail: `lines` holds stance per link (supports / contradicts) and an optional `warrant`: why this evidence bears on this claim. Strength is not stored; it comes from each evidence record's kind. The docs line is marked indirect.

blocks.title: Proposed level-1 fields
blocks.text:
# evidence/evidence.schema.md (sketch)
required: [kind, observed, harness]
properties:
  kind:          enum [run, source, help-text, changelog, docs, issue, third-party, inferred]
  reference:     x-ref references     (required unless kind is run or inferred)
  experiment:    x-ref experiments    (required when kind is run)
  harness:       x-ref harnesses
  version:       string
  version_basis: enum [exact, inferred, unknown]
  observed:      date                 when we looked
  source_date:   date                 the source's own date, if it has one
  locator:       { section | line | timestamp | commit | path }
  excerpt:       { exact, prefix?, suffix? }
  archive:       uri                  a Wayback snapshot, or a file in the corpus
  observed_by:   string               person, or agent + session
  run:           { id, environment, outcome, transcript, sha256 }

steps.title: `kind` is ranked by directness

anchor.exact: kind:          enum [run, source, help-text, changelog, docs, issue, third-party, inferred]

steps.summary: Alpha's enum plus `issue` and `third-party`, listed strongest first for behaviour claims.
steps.detail: For policy claims ("deprecated", "recommended") docs and changelog rank first, because a run cannot show intent. Like system-model's `tier`, a claim is as strong as its best supporting line; no number is stored.

steps.title: Locators are typed and pinned

anchor.exact: locator:       { section | line | timestamp | commit | path }

steps.summary: Where in the reference. Source code is pinned to a commit, never `main`.
steps.detail: Field names follow CSL-JSON's locator types.

steps.title: Two dates, not one
steps.summary: `observed` is when we looked; `source_date` is the page's own date.
steps.detail: Alpha conflates them. Wikipedia's cite web and CSL keep them apart.

steps.title: The quote, re-findable
steps.detail: A `recheck` verb could refetch the page and report present / moved / gone, like Hypothes.is.

steps.title: A snapshot against link rot

anchor.exact: archive:       uri                  a Wayback snapshot, or a file in the corpus

steps.summary: Optional. A Wayback URL carries its own timestamp (a Memento URI-M).
steps.detail: Vendor docs pages are rewritten without notice.

steps.title: Who looked

anchor.exact: observed_by:   string               person, or agent + session

steps.summary: Keeps human-checked and agent-extracted evidence apart.
steps.detail: OKF separates `generated` from `verified`; ECO separates manual from automatic assertion.

blocks.title: Proposed level-2 shape and the spec addition it needs
blocks.text:
experiments/agents-md-read/
├── agents-md-read.md     id, question, claims tested, harnesses + version range,
│                         expected result per claim, controls, safety, maturity
├── setup.sh
├── run.sh
├── validate.sh           output → verdict per claim
├── teardown.sh
├── fixtures/             inputs; hashed per run
└── runs/<run id>/        transcript and outputs

S-GFFY addition (folder records):
  A folder inside a type folder that holds a file named after the folder
  (agents-md-read/agents-md-read.md) is one record. Its id is the folder name.
  Every other file under that folder is an attachment of the record: not a
  record, not checked against the schema, allowed in any format.

steps.title: The record's frontmatter

anchor.exact: ├── agents-md-read.md     id, question, claims tested, harnesses + version range,

steps.summary: What is asked, which claims it tests, and what is expected.
steps.detail: `maturity` follows ACM's artifact badges: draft → functional → reusable → reproduced. Reproduced means a second person, machine, agent session or harness version got the same verdict.

steps.title: Fixed stages
steps.summary: Popper convention: setup, run, validate, teardown.
steps.detail: Fixed names let a tool re-run any experiment when a new harness version ships.

steps.title: A verdict per claim
steps.summary: Turns raw output into supports / contradicts / inconclusive for each claim.
steps.detail: The verdict becomes the stance on the claim's evidence line.

steps.title: Each run leaves a record
steps.summary: Raw output stays here; the run's level-1 evidence record points at it with a hash.
steps.detail: This is the writer D-ORMG asks for.

steps.title: Folder records in S-GFFY
steps.summary: Today a `.sh` or `.txt` file inside a type folder is fine, but a `.json` output in a markdown-only corpus is an error, and nothing ties the files to one record.
steps.detail: Same naming rule as `<type>/<type>.schema.md`, so it reads the same way in a file browser.

steps.label: Find or create the reference
steps.reason: Looks up `references/` by URL; creates `references/Anthropic/Claude Code memory docs.md` if missing.

steps.label: Fetch the page and ask for a Wayback snapshot
steps.reason: Stores `archive` and `url_status`. A failed snapshot is a warning, not an error.

steps.label: Store the quoted text
steps.reason: The person or agent picks the quote; the tool stores `exact` plus 32 characters either side.

steps.label: Write the evidence record
steps.reason: `evidence/Claude Code/2026-11-05 memory docs.md`, then `validate` runs on it.

questions.prompt: Are a page and an observation of it two types?

options.label: Two types: `references` (the page) and `evidence` (one look at it)
options.detail: A page is checked many times; each look keeps its own date, version and quote. Matches the sdlc reference entity and Wikidata's split.

options.label: One `evidence` type with the URL inline
options.detail: Fewer files. Page facts such as its archive repeat in every record.

options.label: On the claim→evidence link, with an optional warrant
options.detail: One run can support one claim and contradict another. SEPIO, Micropublications.

options.label: On the evidence record
options.detail: Simpler, but forces one stance per evidence record.

questions.prompt: Do we store a strength or confidence value?

options.label: No. Derive it from `kind`, ranked by directness, with one ladder for behaviour claims and one for policy claims
options.detail: OKF, system-model, GRADE. An override on a link needs a written reason.

options.label: Yes, a `strength` field on each evidence record
options.detail: Explicit, but hand-entered and goes stale.

options.label: Alpha's list plus `issue` and `third-party`
options.detail: run, source, help-text, changelog, docs, issue, third-party, inferred. Fits harness evidence.

options.label: system-model's list exactly
options.detail: manifest, dependency, files, content. Shared with osdlc, but about repos, not harness behaviour.

options.label: Optional; `validate` warns when a non-run record has none
options.detail: Lets a bare reference-level look land now and be filled in later.

options.label: Required on every non-run record
options.detail: Stronger records; more work per capture.

questions.prompt: How do we guard against link rot?

options.label: Optional `archive` (a Wayback URL) and `url_status`
options.detail: Cheap; the snapshot carries its own date.

options.label: Nothing for now
options.detail: Simplest; pages vanish.

options.label: Capture the page as a file in the corpus, with sha256
options.detail: Fully local; large and copyright-sensitive.

questions.prompt: Can an evidence record be edited after it is written?

options.label: No. Corrections and later results are new records
options.detail: A history of what we saw stays intact; `until` comes from a later contradicting record. Nanopublications.

options.label: Yes
options.detail: Fewer files; history only in git.

questions.prompt: When do folder records enter S-GFFY?

options.label: Now, with this work
options.detail: Experiments need them, and the rule is small.

options.label: When we build the first experiment
options.detail: Keeps S-GFFY unchanged until then.

questions.prompt: How does a claim point at its evidence?

options.label: Each claim is a record with a top-level `evidence` list
options.detail: Works with S-GFFY v0's `x-ref` as is.

options.label: Keep observations nested in a fact; add nested `x-ref` to S-GFFY
options.detail: Closer to alpha; changes the standard.

options.label: By publisher: `references/Anthropic/…`
options.detail: One folder per vendor; easy to browse.

options.label: Flat
options.detail: Simplest; a long list.

options.label: By harness
options.detail: Fits harness pages; awkward for pages about several harnesses.

options.label: A `capture` verb: fetch a page, snapshot it, store a quote
options.detail: Most evidence today is docs. Small to build.

options.label: Experiment runs
options.detail: The strongest evidence, but needs folder records and a runner first.
